content:
Every programmer remembers the excitement of creating their first real web application. After spending time learning Python through small command-line projects, I decided it was finally time to build something people could actually use in a browser.

This project started as a simple idea: create a personal blog where articles can be written, edited, viewed, and deleted. Instead of using a database, each article is stored as an individual JSON file. Although this is not how large websites work, it is an excellent way to understand file handling before moving on to SQL databases.

One of the biggest lessons was learning how Flask routes work. At first I tried to put everything into a single page, but separating the application into multiple routes made the code much easier to understand. Each page now has a clear responsibility: the home page lists articles, the editor creates new ones, and dedicated pages display or modify existing articles.

Another challenge was passing information between HTML templates and Python. Jinja templates made this possible by allowing variables such as the article title, content, and publication date to be displayed dynamically.

There are still many features to add. User authentication, searching, categories, comments, and image uploads are all planned for future versions. Eventually, the project will also be migrated from JSON files to a proper database.

Even though the application is still simple, every new feature teaches an important concept. Looking back at the first version compared to the current one makes it clear how much progress can be made by building projects step by step rather than trying to create a perfect application from the beginning.
title: First article
